Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume XI,
                    South Asia Crisis, 1971
313. Backchannel Message From the Ambassador to Pakistan (
Farland
) to the Presidentʼs
                        Assistant for National Security Affairs (
Kissinger
)
1
Islamabad
,
December 15, 1971,
                            1436Z
.
1096. Foreign Secretary called me to Foreign Office 1800 local 15 December.
                        Said reports received from
Bhutto
indicate he highly pessimistic that any affirmative action will be
                        forthcoming from Security Council. In addition,
GOP
intelligence indicates
GOI
upping offensive activity against West Pakistan and instigating subversive
                        activity (presumably in Pushtun border areas) out of Afghanistan. He said
                        that for West Pakistan to survive as nation it is necessary it be provided
                        additional fighter aircraft. Present trickle MIG–19s and F–104s (he did not
                        indicate origin) cannot stem the tide if India attacks—an attack which
                        Pakistan now expects.
